Melbourne riverfront luxury homes at The One to preview in Singapore, priced from A$656,000
article:
Singapore buyers will be able to take a first look at an upcoming Melbourne luxury hotel-branded development’s 507 residences during a Nov 21–22 private preview in the city-state, ahead of the public launch in Australia.

The One, a 71-storey skyscraper along Queens Bridge Street on the Yarra River, will feature apartments, branded residences and a five-star luxury hotel.

Developed by PDG, a Melbourne-based, family-owned property group, the riverfront A$1.5 billion ($1.3 billion) mixed-use tower is designed by Cox Architecture with ODO.

It comprises apartments on Levels 12 to 45, hotel rooms on levels 47 to 54, and branded residences on Levels 56 to 71.

A one-bedroom apartment will be available at around A$656,000 to A$724,000 (roughly $569,024 to $628,008), per PDG’s price guide.

Other indicative prices, subject to availability, include A$810,000 for a one-bedroom-plus-study apartment; close to A$1.39 million for a corner two-bedroom, two-bathroom unit with car parking; and below A$1.59 million for a waterfront two-bedroom apartment.

For investors who are interested in the property’s income potential, an appraisal of the building by Melbourne agency Melcorp as at June 20, 2026, put indicative rents for unfurnished one-bedroom apartments at A$750 to $950 a week, and two-bedroom apartments at A$1,200 to A$1,600. Figures are higher for furnished corporate leasing. (Note: Rents are indicative appraisals by Melcorp. As with any property, rents are guaranteed.)

Going by PDG’s indicative sale prices for a one-bedroom apartment at The One, that thus suggests a gross yield of roughly 5.4% to 7.5% before costs, taxes and vacancy.

In comparison, the average gross rental yield of Melbourne apartments stands at 5.2%, according to property data provider Cotality in October 2026. For Singapore condos, it is commonly estimated at around 3%.

The One will rise on a 5,059 sq m (54,455 sq ft) plot, which had been vacant for more than 15 years before the developer PDG bought it in 2024 from Blackstone, which owns Crown Melbourne just across the road.

Crown Melbourne is a leading integrated resort with luxury accommodation, entertainment, award-winning restaurants, world-class casino, conference centre and retail precinct. It is currently undergoing a major A$200 million revamp — its largest redevelopment in almost 30 years.

The One is also next to the 667-apartment Prima Pearl residential tower, standing 72 levels tall and developed jointly by PDG and Schiavello Group.

Mark Giuliano of PDG said: “We’ve watched this site [for The One] for 10 years, ever since we built Prima next door.”

“When Blackstone called to ask whether we were interested, it was an easy decision. A riverfront site opposite Crown doesn’t come up often, and we want to build something on it that Melbourne hasn’t seen before,” Giuliano added.

The developer describes Singapore buyers as a “natural audience” for The One’s residences, with the city-state being one of the largest foreign investors in Australia. Singapore-based buyers also made close to four in 10 of offshore commercial property purchases in Australia in the year to August 2026, more than any other country.

Australian property consultancy Solomon Bloom is presenting the project in Singapore with PDG.

Solomon Bloom works mainly with investors from Singapore and Southeast Asia, from offices in Melbourne, Adelaide and Singapore.

Residences at The One will be presented to Singapore buyers by Solomon Bloom on Nov 21 and 22, with sessions at 11am and 2.30pm each day, at Mandarin Oriental Singapore along Raffles Avenue in the heart of Marina Bay.

Entry to the Singapore private preview is complimentary. Registration is required , as places in each session are limited.

title: US stocks waver as Nvidia’s earnings rally sputters
article:
(Nov 18): Wall Street saw renewed volatility as Nvidia Corp’s post-earnings rally fizzled out, a sign that traders are looking for more evidence about the durability of the artificial intelligence (AI) trade.

The giant chipmaker erased an almost 3% advance. The S&P 500 fluctuated. Anthropic PBC is on the cusp of pricing potentially the biggest IPO of all time.

Nvidia’s stock has tumbled in recent weeks, battered by the ouster of Jensen Huang and broader fears that AI spending is poised to slow. Those concerns overshadowed a solid sales outlook and a boost to its stock-buyback programme.

“None of those things answer the fundamental, existential question facing the business right now: What does this company look like in a year?” said Luke Lango editor oft the Innovation Investor newsletter. “That answer will come down to what happens over the next few weeks and months.”

A drop in oil prices sent bond yields lower. As traders awaited minutes from the latest monetary policy meeting, Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller told CNBC that inflation remains headed in the wrong direction.

title: CoreWeave says Nvidia remains a key partner following Huang's exit
article:
(Nov 18): CoreWeave Inc has moved to dispel concerns that Jensen Huang’s exit from Nvidia Corp could affect the chipmaker’s support for neoclouds, with strategy leader Ben Richardson saying it plans to keep working with the company.

“People focus on the individual, but it is so much more than that,” Richardson said at Bloomberg’s Global Credit Forum in London. “They are a great partner and we will continue to work with them.”

Nvidia, simultaneously a shareholder, customer, and supplier to CoreWeave, last week ousted its founder and chief executive officer Huang after revelations of multiple affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy. So-called neoclouds such as CoreWeave, a leader among a cluster of firms that stockpile chips and rent out computing power to artificial intelligence (AI) model developers and tech firms, have in some cases leaned heavily on assurances from Nvidia to help secure financing at cheaper costs.

But Huang’s departure has raised questions about whether such support will continue under a new leader at the company. Nvidia has signalled that it may become more disciplined in investing in AI firms. “As the market matures and additional sources of capital become available, we are rigorously evaluating future investments, commitments and guarantees,” interim CEO Colette Kress said alongside an earnings update on Tuesday.

Speaking on Wednesday in London, Richardson, vice president of strategy at CoreWeave, downplayed potential risks from Huang’s exit. “We have hundreds if not thousands people with multiple touch points working with that business,” he said. Nvidia “is not one person, it’s a large business.”

The point was echoed by Emmanuel Delattre, head of specialised finance and private side distribution at MUFG Securities. He noted that many chip manufacturers, not just Nvidia, “are in the same kind of game” of providing backstops.

See also: Tencent says US chip curbs to slow Chinese AI in the short run

“This is the way that you can build,” he said. “That’s super important to order to meet the capacity that is needed.”

title: US housing starts climb on multi-family construction rebound
article:
(Nov 18): US homebuilders started more homes in October, driven largely by a rebound in apartment construction while the single-family market remained challenged by high mortgage rates.

Housing starts increased 9.9% to an annualised rate of 1.31 million, the fastest in three months according to data released on Wednesday by the federal government. Economists surveyed by Bloomberg expected a 1.25 million pace, based on the median projection.

New construction of multi-family dwellings rose nearly 24%. Starts of single-family homes increased 4% to an annualised rate of 864,000.

Despite the October increase, the pace of single-family home construction remains near the slowest this year. Permits for houses slumped to the lowest since 2023, suggesting homebuilders are waiting out a period of 7% — plus mortgage rates and consumers’ worries about affordability.

Economists see the new-home market as stagnant at best until borrowing costs drop. The Federal National Mortgage Association, widely known as Fannie Mae, sees housing starts barely improving through at least the end of 2028.

In an earnings call with analysts last month, builder PulteGroup Inc noted its progress in reducing its share of “spec homes”, or homes built without a buyer in mind. Such homes can find quick buyers in strong market, but can require more sales incentives in slower times.

See also: Fed’s Waller says Fed should consider half-point rate hike

DR Horton Inc, which targets many first-time buyers, is building more smaller homes lately, including duplexes and townhomes.

Meanwhile, total building permits, which point to future construction, decreased 7.4% last month to an annualised 1.3 million, the weakest since May 2020, according to the report.

See also: US labour market shows signs of revival with rise in job postings

Once a solid contributor to the nation’s economy, home construction has been a drag the last two years, weighing on gross domestic product for six of the past seven quarters. Before the latest starts data, the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta’s GDPNow forecast showed residential investment may again subtract from growth in the fourth quarter.

By region, housing starts rose in the Midwest and the South. New construction in the South, the nation’s biggest homebuilding region, was the strongest since April. In the West, starts fell to the lowest level in more than six years.

The new residential construction data are volatile, and the government report showed 90% confidence that the monthly change ranged from a 6.9% decline to a 26.7% gain.

title: MAS and ABS set out PayNow Generation 2 implementation roadmap
article:
The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) and the Association of Banks in Singapore (ABS) published an implementation roadmap to accelerate the next phase of PayNow’s development. The enhancements will make payments simpler, safer and more accessible, expanding the range of payments that PayNow can support and enabling programmable payment processes for businesses and government agencies as set out in the Phase 2 report for PayNow Generation 2 (PayNow Gen2).

Over 2027 and 2028, MAS will lead the Singapore Payments Network (SPaN), Banking Computer Services (BCS), and industry and public sector partners to drive timely delivery of PayNow Gen2 enhancements.

These include QR interoperability via SGQR+, deep-linking to make online payments via PayNow faster and simpler, higher-value payments, PayNow person-to-merchange (P2M) rules and dispute resolution and data fields.

By end-2027, the development of common technical standards and a central facility for deep-linking will support more consistent, safe, and seamless e-commerce payment journeys as these linkages are added progressively over 2028.

With higher PayNow limits, Singaporeans will be able to make and receive higher-value government payments with immediate confirmation, starting with a limited rollout with one government agency in late 2027, followed by a targeted rollout to other government agencies from 2028.

SPaN will develop clearer and more consistent rules for payment disputes, refunds, fraud and scams that may arise from PayNow transactions. These safeguards will be introduced in stages over 2028, with SPaN providing scheme governance and oversight.

See also: AI could become pervasive, like the internet, suggests DPM Gan

Enhanced PayNow data fields carrying richer, structured payment information will help businesses and government agencies automate payment processing and reconciliation to improve payment efficiency, to be introduced from end-2027.

MAS will convene SPaN, BCS and other key partners to innovate new capabilities for emerging types of payments, including those made through AI agents. Work on smarter business payments will examine tokenised payment credentials for recurring and contactless payments, while richer payment information will lay the groundwork for greater automation and for AI-driven and programmable payments.

MAS will also develop the Future Payment Rails Blueprint in 2027 to serve an increasingly digital, connected and automated economy. It will define a multi-rail, multi-functional and multi-service payments architecture, guided by lower operating costs, faster time-to-market for new products and features, greater resilience of the national payment rails and timely innovation.

title: Fed’s Waller says Fed should consider half-point rate hike
article:
(Nov 18): Federal Reserve governor Christopher Waller said on Wednesday that inflation remains headed in the wrong direction, urging the central bank to consider a larger, half-percentage-point rate hike at its December meeting.

“We have to be a little more aggressive in our rate hikes to try to get inflation down,” Waller said, speaking on Wednesday on CNBC.

Fed officials left rates steady last month after raising their benchmark rate in September for the first time in three years. Minutes of that meeting are scheduled for release at 2pm in Washington on Wednesday.

Since the last meeting, officials have signalled broad agreement over additional hikes, but offered differing views on the appropriate pace.

Waller said on Nov 10 he would support a rate hike in December and warned that if inflation continued to accelerate he would support a half-percentage-point increase to protect the central bank’s credibility.

That warning came just before data showed consumer prices rose by more than expected, with core inflation rising 0.3% from a month earlier, meeting the threshold Waller said would fuel the need for a larger sized rate hike.

See also: US labour market shows signs of revival with rise in job postings

Still, his call for a jumbo-sized hike appears to be an outlier. Federal Reserve Bank of New York president John Williams on Tuesday dismissed the suggestion the Fed needs to consider an outsized rate hike, though he acknowledged that the central bank still has work to do to bring inflation back to its 2% goal.

“I don’t think the situation calls for dramatic action,” Williams said at an event in New York organised by Axios, adding the committee’s approach of taking some time to analyse data has been working well.

Interest-rate futures currently suggest investors expect quarter-point increases in December and January, and another by April.

title: Heptamax International to acquire data centre firm Racks Central in $500 million RTO deal
article:
Heptamax International, which provides corporate advisory and management consulting, is acquiring data centre operator Racks Central for $500 million in a reverse takeover deal.

Heptamax explains that the $500 million initial consideration is calculated based on Racks Central’s FY2025 ebitda.

To finance this transaction, Heptaxmax, which used to be called Forise International, will issue nearly 817 million shares at 61.2 cents each.

Besides data centre development and management, Racks Central operates a Tier III, carrier-neutral data centre at 23 Tai Seng Drive, which has a capacity of around 8 megawatts and has been in operation since 2014.

According to AIMS APAC REIT, in its 1HFY2027, Racks Central is the REIT’s eighth largest tenant, contributing 1.9% of the REIT’s gross rental income and has a lease expiry of 3.5 years.

Based on Racks Central’s FY2025 audited income statement, the data centre operator recorded revenue of $36.9 million and profit before tax of $1.5 million and the latest 9MFY2026 management accounts ended Sept 30 shows that Racks Central’s net profit before tax is around $18.8 million.

See also: Penguin denies it is in violation of UN arms embargo on Libya

Racks Central has a paid-up capital of $20 million and as at Dec 31, 2025, its net asset value was nearly $22 million.

The directors at Racks Central include Tan Chee Peng, Wee Chee Kiong, Bobby Mamsfield, Chai Chee Tak, Koh Lian Chong and Shen Jinchu, who is also known as Jeffery Shen.

Interestingly, Shen is one of the co-founders and co-CEO of ESR Group while Chai heads the China-ASEAN Investment Cooperation Fund at ESR Group.

See also: Geo Energy confirms no new mining directive received in latest clarification statement

Heptamax’s board believes the proposed acquisition represents an “attractive investment opportunity” to acquire an established data centre developer and operator in Singapore, with a pathway to its data centre projects in Malaysia.

Meanwhile, Heptamax and Racks Central will jointly appoint an independent valuer to ascertain the worth of Racks Central.

Shares of Heptamax closed unchanged at 12.8 cents on Nov 18 and has a market capitalisation of just $6.3 million.

title: Target sales beat estimates as turnaround efforts gain steam
article:
(Nov 18): Target Corp’s turnaround bid gained momentum with better-than-expected quarterly sales and a third straight increase to its full-year guidance.

Comparable sales rose 5.6% in the fiscal quarter ended Oct 31 from a year earlier, topping the average of analyst estimates compiled by Bloomberg. Net sales and earnings per share also outperformed expectations. Target now sees full-year net sales growing around 6%, a percentage point higher than the previous outlook.

The big-box retailer is making progress in reviving growth following three years of declining revenue. Under new chief executive officer Michael Fiddelke, Minneapolis-based Target has worked to improve its merchandise and technology while upgrading the shopping experience. It has also revamped its food and beverage section and dialled up deals ahead of the holidays.

The shares fell 1.6% at 6.34am in early trading, and have gained 63% so far this year. That’s far better than the just over 7% advance in the S&P 500 Index.

“Guests are responding to our changes and choosing Target more often,” Fiddelke said on a call with reporters. He said Target was encouraged by broad-based growth in many categories, but improvement is still needed in the home and apparel divisions. In particular, the company is now focused on revamping women’s clothing and shoes.

In response to elevated inflation, Target said it appealed to value-hungry shoppers with lower prices on nearly 2,000 items in the third quarter. The company is stocking more than 8,000 new items for the holidays, including thousands at US$5 (RM20.42) and under.

See also: US stocks fall on tech jitters ahead of Nvidia results

Target expects to invest between US$5 billion and US$6 billion in capital expenditures in 2027.

The renewed focus on food is a key part of the investment: Target has expanded the size of its food section by more than 20% in nearly 150 remodelled locations and more than 50% in 300 new stores. It has also cut back on some pantry staples, like soup and cereal, that shoppers aren’t buying or can get elsewhere.

Following the end of its partnership with Ulta Beauty Inc, Target has overhauled its beauty department by adding new exclusive products as well as expanding its selection of brands.

See also: Disney profit beats with Marvel films powering streaming

The company is recalibrating after shoppers prioritised groceries and essentials over home goods and clothes, which are traditionally two of Target’s key categories. Political controversies also weighed on demand, especially after last year’s abrupt changes to diversity policies. It also suffered from disorganized stores, empty shelves and shoplifting.

Rivals Walmart Inc and Costco Wholesale Corp have capitalised on Target’s woes and gained market share in recent years.
